subject: Performance SLO & Concurrency follow-up / Acme AI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & concurrency (post-call recap)

Hi Alex — great conversation this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can map to Redwood capacity/pricing: 

Summary of what we heard
- Target p95 generation latency: ~200ms for short completions (<=256 tokens).
- Streaming required for live transcription pipeline (partial tokens to downstream worker).
- Expected traffic shape: baseline ~50 concurrent requests, peak bursts to ~150 concurrent requests for short periods, and scheduled batch inference windows (nightly).
- Per-customer request patterns: many short requests (~50–200 tokens) and occasional long completions (~1k tokens).

Questions for sizing/quote
1) Can you confirm peak sustained concurrency (requests in flight) vs. instantaneous parallelism (connections)? Our sizing differs based on whether connections are pooled or each request opens a new connection.
2) Do you expect many long-running streaming connections (open >60s)? If so, what proportion of peak concurrency are these?
3) Any hard SLOs for availability/latency (e.g., 99th/95th targets) that we should bake into a dedicated pool SLA?

Next steps
- If you can share the small SLO/traffic worksheet (attached) with expected hourly distribution and a sample request size breakdown, I’ll run this through our capacity planner and get back with: estimate (tokens/sec), recommended concurrency quota, and two options: hosted increase vs. Dedicated pool with reserved capacity and a firm SLA.
- Proposed next sync: 30 min on Tue to cap the concurrency and streaming requirements.

Attaching: acme-slo-requirements.xlsx (worksheet for traffic/latency targets).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0183

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Barker <tim@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & concurrency (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side after a quick internal sync: 

- Concurrency: our expected peak "requests in flight" is closer to 300 for major product events (promos). Day-to-day peak is ~120–150. Average concurrent active callers is ~40–60.
- Connections: we plan to use connection pooling from our side; typical pool size per process is 200 sockets. We expect around 10–20 app instances hitting Redwood at peak, so total simultaneous TCP connections could be high if you limit connection reuse.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for live transcription — roughly 20% of sessions will be long-running streams (>60s), the rest are short streaming bursts for partials (~5–10s).
- Latency SLOs: p95 end-to-end generation latency target is 250ms for short completions. For long streaming sessions we care more about throughput and stability than strict token latency.
- Availability: we are looking for 99.9% or better for production traffic.

We are evaluating two routes: 1) increase hosted quota + elevated rate limits for the account, or 2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) if carrier-grade SLAs and predictable throughput are needed. Cost sensitivity: we expect higher token volume but want to avoid large overprovisioning.

Attached: quick numbers from our infra team (I pasted them below into the worksheet).

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, Acme AI
alex.johnson@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & concurrency (post-call recap)

Appreciate the detail, Alex — that's helpful and clarifies a few points. Quick notes from Redwood and options for you: 

Sizing notes
- For peak 300 concurrent requests with 20% long-running streams, the dominant cost is socket concurrency + KV cache behavior. Our hosted path has hard rate limits per account by default (requests/min and concurrent-in-flight tokens) but those can be raised via a quota request or by moving to a Dedicated pool.
- Connection pooling: if your app reuses outbound connections, that dramatically reduces per-connection overhead. If each of your 10–20 app instances uses a pool of ~25 concurrent requests (rather than 200), we can meet peak without Dedicated in many cases.

Options
1) Hosted quota increase (fast): we can raise your concurrent request quota to 350 and requests/min to 10k for a short pilot. This includes temporary soft limits and a monitoring window. No SLA change; rate-limit exceptions handled via traffic shaping and fallbacks.
2) Dedicated pool (recommended at scale): reserved capacity sized for 300 concurrent with a 99.9% SLA, connection/streaming guarantees, and predictable per-token pricing. Includes canary rollout and a plan for graceful degradation to a smaller hosted variant if capacity is constrained.

Suggested mutual action plan (MAP) + next steps
- You: share final hourly traffic profile in the attached worksheet and confirm whether you can reduce per-process connection pools OR provide a proxy that multiplexes requests.
- Redwood: we’ll run a cost + capacity plan and return: recommended concurrency quota, expected p95 latency at your request sizes, and a proposed pilot/price.
- Joint call: Tue 2026-04-14 10:00 PT to finalize MAP and sign off on pilot sizes.

I’ve attached our rate limits overview and a draft MAP for review (redwood-rate-limits-overview.pdf, draft-mutual-action-plan.docx). If you prefer we can open a formal quota case to expedite the increase — I can spin that up after we confirm traffic numbers.

If this looks good I’ll also loop in pricing (Neha) and infra (Aditya) for the pilot and Dedicated sizing.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0183
